# AI-Ready Design Systems

> A curated, scored catalog of 230 production-grade design systems (web, iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native) for AI agents. Use it to pick the best design systems for a product idea, then build the product with the chosen system. Every entry passed a quality gate (actively maintained, real adoption) and is scored for AI-readiness (MCP server, llms.txt, machine-readable tokens, typed APIs, registry install).

Updated 2026-11-05. Machine-readable catalog: https://kindavishal.github.io/ai-ready-design-systems/catalog.json. Every system has a page at https://kindavishal.github.io/ai-ready-design-systems/systems/<slug>.md with install, theming, AI resources and a build guide.

## How to use this (instructions for agents)

When a user asks you to find design systems for a product idea:

1. **Understand the product.** Extract or ask (max 3 short questions, only if it changes the answer):
   - Platform(s): web, iOS, Android, cross-platform, desktop.
   - Existing stack / framework, if any (React/Next.js, Vue/Nuxt, Angular, Svelte, Flutter, SwiftUI, Compose, React Native, Blazor…). If none, you may recommend one.
   - Product type and audience (e.g. B2B dashboard, consumer app, e-commerce, AI chat, government service, internal tool, marketing site).
   - Brand needs: use a system's look as-is, light theming, or a fully custom brand (favour headless or copy-the-source systems for full custom).
   - Constraints: accessibility/regulation level, density (data-heavy vs. spacious), license, Tailwind or not.
2. **Filter** https://kindavishal.github.io/ai-ready-design-systems/catalog.json by platform and framework. Exclude systems whose ecosystem tags (`*-ecosystem`) or `government` tag don't fit the product.
3. **Rank** the rest. Weigh, in order: fit with product type and audience (`tags`, `bestFor`), fit with stack and styling, `tier` (recommended > solid > watch), `aiReadiness`, `popularity`.
4. **Read the page** (`page` URL) of your top candidates to confirm fit and caveats ("Consider an alternative if").
5. **Answer with the top 3**: for each, one line on why it fits, the main trade-off, AI-readiness score, and the link to its page. Say which one you recommend and why. Mention when a specialised system should be *combined* with a base system (e.g. AI Elements or assistant-ui for chat on top of shadcn/ui; Tremor for charts).
6. **Build** once the user picks (or immediately if they asked you to build):
   - Open the system page and follow its **Install** and **Setup** sections.
   - Connect its MCP server if one is listed, and read its `llms.txt`; prefer these over memory, since APIs change between major versions.
   - Apply the user's brand through the theme/tokens API once at the root, then follow the page's **Build checklist**.

## Scoring

- **Quality gate (to be listed):** commit, release or package publish in the last 12 months (12–24 months = "watch"); not archived or deprecated; and at least one of ≥1.0k GitHub stars, ≥5.0k weekly npm downloads, ≥300 pub.dev likes, ≥1.0M NuGet downloads, or maintained by a known company/government/institution.
- **AI-readiness (0–100):** Official MCP server (agent can query components/docs live) (20); llms.txt on the docs site (15); llms-full.txt (whole docs as one markdown file) (5); Machine-readable design tokens in the repo (15); Typed component API (TypeScript / Swift / Kotlin / Dart / C#) (10); Registry / CLI install of component source (e.g. shadcn registry) (10); Agent instructions in the repo (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, cursor rules, skills) (5); Storybook / live, inspectable examples (5); Figma Code Connect (design ↔ code mapping) (5); Accessibility guidance shipped with the source (5); Dedicated documentation site (5).
- **Tiers:** recommended = passes gate and AI-readiness ≥ 45 (platform-native systems always qualify); solid = passes gate; watch = maintenance slowing.

## Reference only (closed source — inspiration, not installable)

- Stripe Apps UI Toolkit (Stripe): https://docs.stripe.com/stripe-apps/components — Only usable inside Stripe Apps.
- Linear (Linear): https://linear.app — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
- Vercel Geist (Vercel): https://vercel.com/geist/introduction — Docs and fonts public; component code not published.
- ServiceNow Horizon (ServiceNow): https://horizon.servicenow.com — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
- BBC GEL (BBC): https://www.bbc.co.uk/gel — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
- Tailwind Plus (Tailwind UI / Catalyst) (Tailwind Labs): https://tailwindcss.com/plus — Paid license; agents can only use it if you own a license and provide the source.
- Wise Design (Wise): https://wise.design — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
- Airbnb Design Language (Airbnb): https://airbnb.design — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
- Mailchimp Design System (Intuit Mailchimp): https://ux.mailchimp.com/patterns — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
- HubSpot Canvas (HubSpot): https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/platform/ui-extensions — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
- Duolingo Design (Duolingo): https://design.duolingo.com — Closed source: use for inspiration only.
